headline: US diesel breaks $6/gallon for the first time as war risk premium builds
intro: Diesel just smashed through a psychological ceiling nobody wanted to see, and it's not stopping to catch its breath. With crack spreads north of $100 and Hormuz talk swirling, the pain is about to show up in everyone's freight bill.
overview: National average diesel prices topped $6/gallon for the first time ever, per AAA and GasBuddy, as Middle East tensions—including a Houthi seizure of Perim island and reports of Saudi crude disruptions—drove Brent above $100 and diesel cracks to $106.44/bbl. Gasoline cracks also firmed to $40.88/bbl even as broader crude markets showed signs of pausing after a historic rally, with IEA cutting demand forecasts amid war-driven demand destruction. On the policy and clean-fuels side, IRS guidance on the 45Z credit, feedstock deals (Bayer-Neste canola), and refinery clean-fuels investments (OMV Petrom, Twelve's AirPlant One financing) continued to move forward against this volatile backdrop.

decks.title: 8-K exhibit ex991sunandsuncdelistnysel.htm (filed 2026-09-10)
decks.analysis:
## Key Takeaways

- **No operational or financial disclosures**: This 8-K exhibit is exclusively an administrative announcement regarding a stock exchange listing transfer (NYSE → Texas Stock Exchange), effective October 5, 2026. It contains no data on throughput, utilization, capture rates, margins, or guidance.

- **No renewable fuels or RIN/LCFS content**: The filing does not address renewable diesel, SAF economics, capacity, or RIN/LCFS exposure in any capacity.

- **No capital allocation signals**: There is no mention of capex, distributions, buybacks, or balance sheet actions tied to this transfer.

- **Business description reiterated (unchanged)**: The filing repeats standard descriptive figures — ~14,000 miles of pipeline, 170+ terminals, >15 billion gallons distributed annually, ~11,000 retail locations across 33 countries/territories — but these are boilerplate "About Sunoco" figures, not new operational metrics or guidance updates.

- **Corporate/ticker mechanics only**: SUN and SUNC will retain identical ticker symbols on TXSE; no unitholder action is required, and the transfer is framed as aligning with SUN/SUNC's Texas-based operational footprint.

## Market Signal

This filing is not fuels-market-relevant news: it signals only an exchange-listing/venue change for SUN and SUNC's common units, and refined-products traders should not draw any inference about throughput, margins, or renewable fuels economics from it.

decks.title: 8-K exhibit tm2625060d1_ex99-1.htm (filed 2026-09-11)
decks.analysis:
## Fuel-Segment Extract: Kroger 2Q26 (period ended Aug 15, 2026)

- **No fuel gallon volumes, fuel comps, or station count data disclosed** in this release — all identical sales metrics (0.2% Q2, 3.4% prior year) are reported *excluding* fuel.
- **Fuel cited as a margin mix headwind**: overall gross margin declined to 22.4% (from 22.5%) partly due to "the mix effect of higher fuel sales" alongside higher shrink and transportation costs.
- **Fuel called out as an EPS tailwind**: CFO David Kennerley attributed adjusted EPS growth (+5%) in part to "strong pharmacy and fuel performance," alongside cost savings and eCommerce profitability gains — but no margin rate or dollar figure was quantified.
- **Total sales including fuel rose to $34.6B from $33.9B**, while sales excluding fuel (and adjusting for Vitacost sale/fulfillment center exits) grew just 0.1%, implying fuel sales dollars were a meaningful contributor to the topline increase, though volume/price split is not broken out.
- No commentary on membership-fuel programs, fuel center openings/closures, or fuel-specific capital allocation.

**Signal for fuels markets:** Kroger's fuel business appears to have benefited from higher fuel sales dollars (likely price-driven given no volume disclosure) and contributed positively to profitability, but the company provides no granular fuel margin, gallon, or station data — limiting this release's utility as a fuels-market indicator beyond confirming fuel remained a net-positive, low-margin-mix drag on retail gross margin.
